badges.name: Otter Point Park
badges.blurb: Stand on low coastal rock beside a wind-shaped conifer above the Juan de Fuca Strait.

badges.name: Lookout Lake Park
badges.blurb: A quiet pebble shore meets the small, wooded waters of Lookout Lake.

badges.name: Havenwood Park
badges.blurb: Timber steps climb through the green woodland of Havenwood Park.

badges.name: Herm Williams Park
badges.blurb: Two distinctive dark pergolas stand amid the lawn and tall firs.

badges.name: Esquimalt Lagoon Park
badges.blurb: A narrow sand and gravel spit shelters Esquimalt Lagoon from the Strait, leaving a shallow tidal lagoon where herons, shorebirds, and seasonal waterfowl feed. The forested far shore and distinct open and sheltered waters give this sanctuary its recognizable shape.

badges.name: Outlook Park
badges.blurb: Climb to a small arbutus-framed lookout above Colwood and the sea.

badges.name: Latoria Creek Park
badges.blurb: Timber-railed steps climb through the cedar and fir woods of Latoria Creek Park.

badges.name: Glen Lake Beach Park
badges.blurb: Relax by the small sandy beach, then take in Glen Lake from the timber pier.

badges.name: Willing Park
badges.blurb: Follow the gravel loop beside a quiet pond and its small white truss bridge.

badges.name: Langford Lake Park
badges.blurb: Walk the Ed Nixon boardwalk beside Langford Lake, where sheltered wetlands meet open water and wooded hills.

badges.name: Lake Ida Anne
badges.blurb: Circle the small tree-lined fishing pond, with its brushy island and low fountain.

badges.name: Beacon Hill Park
badges.blurb: Garden paths, roaming peacocks and the stone bridge over Goodacre Lake make Beacon Hill a place to wander. Garry oak meadows shelter sensitive native plants, while the park's southern edge opens onto the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Nearby Mile Zero marks the western end of the Trans-Canada Highway.

badges.name: Banfield Park
badges.blurb: Follow the Gorge shoreline to Banfield Park and its expanded swim dock, where floating platforms reach into calm water below the wooded bank.

badges.name: Holland Point Park
badges.blurb: Holland Point Park is a breathtaking 13.8-acre oceanfront greenspace located along Dallas Road in Victoria's historic James Bay neighbourhood. It is known for its sweeping, unobstructed views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and the snow-capped Olympic Mountains across the water.

badges.name: Clover Point Park
badges.blurb: Clover Point juts into the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with a rocky tip, curved pebble shore and broad views across the water.

badges.name: Moss Rocks Park
badges.blurb: Climb the exposed mossy rock hill for a view over Fairfield and the Strait.

badges.name: Summit Park
badges.blurb: Spring crocuses brighten the open Garry oak meadow at Summit Park.

badges.name: Cecelia Ravine Park
badges.blurb: Green-railed stairs climb through the leafy Cecelia Ravine.

badges.name: Butterfield Park
badges.blurb: Follow the quiet woodland path across a short plank beside mossy logs and cedars.

badges.name: Verdier Park
badges.blurb: Reach the pebble shore by the timber walkway where kayaks meet the sheltered water.

badges.name: Oak Haven Park
badges.blurb: Garry oaks and golden grass crown rocky hilltop views over Saanich Inlet.

badges.name: Eleanor Mann Park
badges.blurb: Follow a narrow grassy connector through pale meadow grass into Metchosin woodland.

badges.name: Carlton Cosh Nature Park
badges.blurb: Find a sunlit grassy opening among the trees at Carlton Cosh Nature Park.

badges.name: Buckbrush Swamp Park
badges.blurb: Look across the broad buckbrush wetland to the forest edge in Buckbrush Swamp Park.

badges.name: Dominion Brook Park
badges.blurb: Stone steps lead through bright rhododendrons in Dominion Brook Park.

badges.name: Patricia Bay Park
badges.blurb: A shoreline path curves above the pebble edge of Patricia Bay.

badges.name: Lillian Hoffar Park
badges.blurb: Follow the short shore steps beneath cedar branches to the calm water at Lillian Hoffar Park.

badges.name: Nymph Point Park
badges.blurb: Peeling red arbutus limbs frame clear, stone-bottomed water at Nymph Point.

badges.name: Bazan Bay Park
badges.blurb: Explore a small North Saanich park by Bazan Bay, where coastal water and wide skies set the scene.

badges.name: Reay Creek Park
badges.blurb: Cross the timber footbridge into the shaded forest beside Reay Creek.

badges.name: Trafalgar Park
badges.blurb: Look down from the rocky bluff over a quiet cove and the open Strait.

badges.name: Anderson Hill Park
badges.blurb: Lichen-marked rock rises above the sea and low offshore islets at Anderson Hill.

badges.name: Willows Park
badges.blurb: Willows Park pairs an open Oak Bay beach with lawns, mature trees, a playground, and the Kiwanis Tea Room. Driftwood and pebbles line the shore below the small beachside building.

badges.name: Uplands Park
badges.blurb: Uplands Park protects an open Garry oak meadow that blooms with camas and other wildflowers in spring. Its shallow rocky ground leads toward Cattle Point and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

badges.name: Cordova Bay Park
badges.blurb: Follow the path through Cordova Bay Park to the beach, where the shore opens onto a broad view of the bay and water beyond.

badges.name: Cuthbert Holmes Park
badges.blurb: Cross the low timber bridge over the Colquitz River, then explore the quiet estuary and bird habitat of Cuthbert Holmes Park.

badges.name: Whitehead Park
badges.blurb: A broad willow shades the open lawn beside Prospect Lake at Whitehead Park.

badges.name: Cadboro Gyro Park
badges.blurb: Cadboro-Gyro Park pairs a sandy Cadboro Bay waterfront with a marine-themed playground. Its red octopus, blue salmon, and green-and-yellow Caddy sea serpent are concrete play sculptures.

badges.name: Gorge Waterway Park
badges.blurb: Tidal water churns through the rocky narrows beneath Tillicum Bridge.

badges.name: Glencoe Cove - Kwatsech Park
badges.blurb: A small pebble cove nestles below the wooded slope at Glencoe Cove - Kwatsech Park.

badges.name: PKOLS (Mount Douglas Park)
badges.blurb: PKOLS, the mountain’s SENĆOŦEN name, is a place of deep importance to the W̱SÁNEĆ. Trails climb through forest to a rocky 225 m summit with sweeping ocean views.

badges.name: Quick's Bottom Park
badges.blurb: Tall grasses spread across the open lowland of this Saanich park.

badges.name: Playfair Park
badges.blurb: Mature rhododendrons and azaleas arch over winding garden paths at Playfair Park. Beyond the blooms, a Garry oak meadow brings camas each spring.

badges.name: Arbutus Cove Park
badges.blurb: A sheltered crescent of rocky shore and sand opens onto blue water.

badges.name: Mount Tolmie Park
badges.blurb: Garry oaks and sunlit rock crown Mount Tolmie, where summit paths open to sweeping views over Greater Victoria and the surrounding mountains.

badges.name: Outerbridge Park
badges.blurb: A low plank bridge crosses a rocky garden stream in Outerbridge Park.

badges.name: Ed Macgregor Park
badges.blurb: Follow the raised Sooke Marine Boardwalk beside Ed Macgregor Park, with sheltered harbour water and wooded shoreline views.

badges.name: Whiffin Spit Park
badges.blurb: Whiffin Spit's level path winds along a narrow, hooked shoreline at the mouth of Sooke Harbour. Its rounded point offers wide views across the harbour and Salish Sea, with coastal plants and marine wildlife along the way.

badges.name: Sooke Bluffs Park
badges.blurb: Timber stairs descend a wooded coastal bluff toward the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

badges.name: Iroquois Park
badges.blurb: Pause by the willow and yellow flowers at the little duck pond in Iroquois Park.

badges.name: Seaport Park
badges.blurb: Flower beds and rope-wrapped timber posts frame a brick waterfront walk in Seaport Park.

badges.name: Resthaven Park
badges.blurb: Follow the curving path across Resthaven Park lawn toward the quiet harbour shore.

badges.name: Welland Legacy Park
badges.blurb: Explore the heritage orchard at Welland Legacy Park, where fruit trees grow beside the paths.

badges.name: Portage Inlet Linear Park
badges.blurb: Follow the curving shore path past shade trees and a picnic table beside Portage Inlet.

badges.name: View Royal Park
badges.blurb: View Royal Park borders the estuary at Craigflower Creek's mouth, where the tidal channel curves beside the open field.

badges.name: Knockan Hill Park
badges.blurb: Climb the rocky knoll beneath arbutus branches for a view across the treetops.

badges.name: Saxe Point Park
badges.blurb: Fir-lined trails and open lawns lead to Saxe Point's rocky beach, with Strait of Juan de Fuca views toward the Olympic Mountains.

badges.name: Macaulay Point Park
badges.blurb: A gravel path follows Macaulay Point's rocky shoreline, with views across the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Inland trails also reach the surviving ramparts of Fort Macaulay.

badges.name: Esquimalt Gorge Park
badges.blurb: Esquimalt Gorge Park's restored Japanese garden brings a wooden gate, footbridge and reflecting pond to the Gorge Waterway.

badges.name: Propeller Park
badges.blurb: See the rusted ship propeller framed by a clipped hedge and stone wall at Propeller Park.

badges.name: Memorial Park
badges.blurb: Walk the tree-lined approach to the Esquimalt cenotaph, framed by two historic field guns.

badges.name: Ƚáuˌwelṉew̱ / John Dean Park
badges.blurb: Walk beneath towering old-growth Douglas-firs in Ƚáuˌwelṉew̱ / John Dean Park. Shaded trails pass mossy trunks and ferns through one of the Saanich Peninsula's last stands of old-growth forest.

badges.name: Bamberton Park
badges.blurb: Bamberton Park opens onto a stony low-tide beach beside Saanich Inlet, with wooded campsites and picnic spots above the shore.

badges.name: Goldstream Park
badges.blurb: Each autumn, salmon return to the Goldstream River beneath old-growth firs and cedars, drawing bald eagles to this South Island park.

badges.name: Gowlland Tod Park
badges.blurb: Gowlland Tod Park's Jocelyn Hill trail climbs through arbutus and rocky forest to views across Finlayson Arm. The narrow inlet winds between wooded slopes below the ridge.

badges.name: Spectacle Lake Park
badges.blurb: A spring-fed lake rests among mature forest and wetlands on the Malahat. Follow the easy loop past wooden creek bridges to a modest sandy shore.

badges.name: Albert Head Lagoon Regional Park
badges.blurb: Explore the cobble beach and driftwood at Albert Head Lagoon, where a rocky shore borders the sheltered lagoon and opens to views of the Olympic Mountains.

badges.name: Bear Hill Regional Park
badges.blurb: Moss-covered rock shelves wind beneath the woodland canopy on Bear Hill.

badges.name: Coles Bay Regional Park
badges.blurb: Weathered driftwood rests beside the calm water of Coles Bay.

badges.name: Devonian Regional Park
badges.blurb: Rounded cobbles meet the calm water at the Devonian coast.

badges.name: East Sooke Regional Park
badges.blurb: Follow East Sooke's rugged Coast Trail past rocky bays and pocket beaches, with views across the Strait of Juan de Fuca to the Olympic Mountains.

badges.name: Elk/Beaver Lake Regional Park
badges.blurb: Elk and Beaver are joined lakes ringed by a 10 km loop, with four beaches, willow-shaded shores, and a rowing centre at Eagle Beach.

badges.name: Francis/King Regional Park
badges.blurb: Follow the Elsie King Trail through Heritage Grove, where old-growth Douglas-firs and the park's Arch Tree shape the forest.

badges.name: Gonzales Hill Regional Park
badges.blurb: Walk the rocky Gonzales Hill summit beside its white observatory, with views over Gonzales Bay and the Salish Sea.

badges.name: Horth Hill Regional Park
badges.blurb: Moss and ferns cover a rugged rock outcrop in the Horth Hill woods.

badges.name: Island View Beach Regional Park
badges.blurb: Island View Beach has a long driftwood-lined shore and pockets of dunes, wetland, and salt marsh. At low tide, shorebirds forage across exposed sand and shallow channels, with James Island and Mount Baker beyond Haro Strait.

badges.name: Lone Tree Hill Regional Park
badges.blurb: A solitary tree rises from the rocky summit above a wide forested view.

badges.name: Matheson Lake Regional Park
badges.blurb: A forested trail circles Matheson Lake, with a small tree-covered island set in its blue water. A sandy beach offers a place to pause along the shore.

badges.name: Mill Hill Regional Park
badges.blurb: Climb through oak and arbutus to the rocky Mill Hill summit, where a stone peak finder overlooks Esquimalt Harbour.

badges.name: Mount Wells Regional Park
badges.blurb: Climb through Douglas-fir and mossy rock to Mount Wells' open summit, where a broad view stretches across Langford toward Victoria.

badges.name: Mount Work Regional Park
badges.blurb: Climb through forest to Mount Work's exposed rocky summit, where moss and lichen mark the stone and broad views open over the surrounding treetops and hills.

badges.name: Roche Cove Regional Park
badges.blurb: Follow forest trails to the sheltered waters and rocky shore of Roche Cove.

badges.name: Sea to Sea Regional Park
badges.blurb: Climb the rocky Mount Manuel Quimper summit for a sweeping view across Sooke Basin and the surrounding forest.

badges.name: Sooke Hills Wilderness Regional Park
badges.blurb: Cross the Goldstream River footbridge into deep forest trails and ridge views in Sooke Hills Wilderness.

badges.name: Sooke Potholes Regional Park
badges.blurb: Swirling water and glacial boulders carved the Sooke River's namesake rock pools, now framed by forest and polished stone ledges.

badges.name: Thetis Lake Regional Park
badges.blurb: Upper and Lower Thetis Lakes pair forested shores and sandy swimming beaches with more than 40 km of trails.

badges.name: Witty's Lagoon Regional Park
badges.blurb: A forest trail passes Sitting Lady Falls and reaches a broad tidal beach, one of the few sandy shores with significant tides on southern Vancouver Island. Witty's Lagoon also shelters more than 160 recorded bird species.
